Microsoft Store Installation

Edit page
This content was created with AI assistance. Please verify important details.

For Windows users, Microsoft Store is the current public desktop entry point. This page covers the Store path only. If you need the broader Desktop download, version-management, and troubleshooting guide, continue with Desktop Installation.

The main Steam app entry has already been retired, so Microsoft Store is now the primary Windows channel. For background, see Why HagiCode is not available on Steam.

Good fit for this path

  • you are on Windows 10 or Windows 11 and want to install directly from the system store
  • you prefer store-delivered app packages instead of handling installer files manually
  • you only need a local personal setup and are not planning a Docker Compose deployment

Before you start

Confirm these conditions first:

  • your device can open the Microsoft Store page for HagiCode for Windows
  • network access is available on first launch because the app may still prepare additional runtime components
  • some devices, regions, or organization policies may ask you to sign in with a Microsoft account first
  • if Store access is blocked on your machine, switch to Desktop Installation

Install from Microsoft Store

  1. Open HagiCode for Windows.
  2. Click Get, Install, or the equivalent action shown by the Store page.
  3. Wait for Microsoft Store to finish downloading and installing the app.
  4. Launch HagiCode from the Start menu or directly from the Store page.

What happens on first launch

After installation, HagiCode still continues through the standard Desktop initialization flow.

  • first launch can be slower than a typical app because the local runtime still needs to be prepared
  • the Microsoft Store / MSIX channel locks some dependency-management and runtime-path settings by design
  • the app does not self-update independently; package delivery depends on the installation channel, and Store delivery is tied to the Microsoft Store channel

If you want to continue with the onboarding flow, read Wizard Setup.

When to use another installation path

Another channel is a better fit when:

  • you cannot access Microsoft Store, or your organization blocks Store installation
  • you need to download .exe or .msix files manually and control the installer source yourself
  • you are deploying to a server, NAS, or team environment, in which case Docker Compose Deployment is the better path

Troubleshooting

The Microsoft Store page does not open

Check system network access, region settings, and Microsoft Store sign-in status first. If the browser link opens but the Store client remains unavailable, the usual cause is local system policy. In that case, switch to Desktop Installation.

Some settings are locked

Store / MSIX installs intentionally lock some dependency-management and runtime-data path options. That is expected behavior for this distribution channel, not an installation failure.

First launch still downloads or prepares more content

The Store package only delivers the desktop application package. On first launch, HagiCode may still check version metadata, prepare local components, or continue default initialization. Keep the network available and wait for the current step to finish.
